prerequisites: Mathematics (Algebra, Vector Calculus, Integral and Differential Calculus, Numerical Methods)

learning_outcomes.text: Students explain the laws of aerodynamics and flight mechanics and describe their areas of application.
Students recognize current trends in developments in aerodynamics and flight mechanics and explain the reasons behind them.
Students carry out design tasks and recalculations as well as wind tunnel tests and numerical simulations.
Students present on the subject area to different audiences.
Students calculate, design, and operate aircraft.
Graduates can apply knowledge and understanding to activities or professions and develop or further develop problem solutions in aerodynamics and flight mechanics.
Students can conceptualize methods and procedures suitable for systematically processing and solving selected problems in aerodynamics and flight mechanics.

Graduates formulate problem solutions in aerodynamics and flight mechanics within their actions and can justify them in discourse with experts and non-experts with theoretically and methodologically sound arguments; they communicate and cooperate with other experts and non-experts to solve a task responsibly; they reflect on and consider different perspectives and interests of other parties.

Graduates develop a professional self-image that is oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields predominantly outside of science; they justify their own professional actions with theoretical and methodological knowledge; they can assess their own abilities, autonomously reflect on subject-specific design and decision-making freedoms and use them under guidance; they recognize contextually appropriate framework conditions of professional action and ethically justify their decisions; they critically reflect on their professional actions in relation to societal expectations and consequences.

syllabus_topics: Aerodynamics of the wing, fuselage, and tail units under subsonic and supersonic flow.
Simplified equations of motion of an aircraft as a rigid body in space.
Solution of the equations for longitudinal and lateral motion.
Estimation of flight performance, flight characteristics, stability, and controllability.
Computer exercises: Numerical calculation of flow over wings and aircraft.
Laboratory practical: Wind tunnel measurements on wings and aircraft.
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is an exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 3-4 experiments.
